hypothesis: A potential-field gradient ridge cannot distinguish an elongated fault/contact from a compact intrusion/vent. The RTP-magnetic (band 2) and isostatic-gravity (band 13) gradient tensors encode dimensionality and a candidate strike. A near-2-D, strike-concordant ridge should preferentially retain fault-like structure. H57-A adds a 15-pixel off-catalogue flank prior built only from the VISIBLE catalogue during holdout, based on the measured adjacency pattern in the local anchor forensics. It was tested as a new-fault prediction, not assumed to be a leaderboard improvement.
mechanism: Use the existing one-scale cached stack (band 2 RTP magnetic + band 13 isostatic gravity); nearest-valid fill, robust line-axis leveling, low-pass before mirror-padded FFT derivatives, closed-form symmetric 3x3 tensor eigendecomposition, dimensionality invariant, intermediate eigenvector strike, strike agreement, plunge weight, corroborated ridge rank. H57 holdout and final writer use the same cached tensor factors and a 15-pixel quadratic off-catalogue flank prior; the candidate sensitivity run removes the cached 6-pixel footprint erosion (un-eroded edge score) to test whether a dense 5-pixel lattice registry raster leaves any unique feasible pixels. Flight-line striping is hard-masked. At run time the final 200 binary dots were placed with 3-pixel minimum separation and 56 registry cover masks, including one misregistered raster reprojected to the official grid, under a 0.68 cap. A later audit added six parallel-session registry variants and four local historical candidates; the current 66-raster strict scan finds 0.76 overlap with two PARALLEL16 twins, so this raster is not unique under the literal rule.
named_non_fault_mimic: Lithologic contacts, dikes, intrusive sheets, basin-margin alluvial edges, and acquisition/FFT edge artifacts can all produce long, near-2-D responses without being faults. Flight-line striping and tie-line/leveling residuals are additional potential mimics. The un-eroded footprint-edge sensitivity increases FFT boundary-ringing risk and is a reason this raster remains audit-only.

holdout_dti.protocol: Five whole-segment/lattice hide-and-recover folds, 3-pixel buffer, per-fold visible faults masked pixel-exactly; flank prior recomputed from VISIBLE faults only; all 56 registry rasters budgeted after alignment to EPSG:32611 template; 40 dots per fold; pooled TP/FP/FN DTI; 95% CI is a 4,000-resample bootstrap of the five fold DTI values. All candidate and comparator arms returned the same requested mass. The holdout used the 56 registry rows present at run time; the later strict uniqueness audit includes 62 registry rows plus four local historical rasters. No holdout was rerun after the three-experiment budget was exhausted.
holdout_dti.promotion_rule: candidate must beat tensor_full, ridge_x_agree, and random, and beat the best surface in >=4/5 folds; all arms must be mass-matched
